When typing the wrong password into any given internet site, is it registered?

The short answer, no, because that's not how passwords work. It depends on the site I guess.

long answer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=22DsoTILS4U

If you are asking if it's possible for a website to record your password so that it can add it to a password list, the answer is yes. If you use the same password on any two accounts, neither is secure. If you have your passwords memorized (and you don't have a photographic memory), your accounts are not secure. Everyone should be using a password manager with unique, randomly generated passwords. 1Password is a fantastic service. If you're looking for something free, use KeePass.

I remember only one password for KeePass and none of my accounts use the same password. My KeePass file is synced to Dropbox so I can get to it from any of my device.

It's pretty great not having to remember passwords anymore.
Thanks, password is pretty un-secure, every service should use some kind of authenticator for safety reason.

A password is plenty secure for the vast majority of stuff you need it for on the internet, provided you choose and use it correctly.

For banking, my primary email address and, say, my Steam account, I definitely want stuff like two-way authentication, but I don't want the hassle of additional authentication for every goddamn forum, video game or other stuff I use. Most importantly I don't want to give every other random website that requires a password more information about me, like, say, a hash key derived from my PC hardware or my cell phone number just so I can get additional authentication.

Are you asking if you can tell if an account name is registered by trying to log in with a fake password? If that's your question, the answer is No, most of the time.

It's pretty much standard security practice to show a vague error message when login fails, like "incorrect username or password". The point is to hide which part of the credentials is wrong, so someone trying random accounts will not know not if it's username or password is wrong.

Of course, some sites don't do this and will show different messages like "incorrect username" or "incorrect email", which makes it easier to brute force accounts.

It depends on what you mean by "registered" and also on the site you're talking about.

Any given site can interpret and use the data you send to it in an infinite number of ways, there is no universal answer to that question.
Any serious system should be on the look out for bot attacks (trying many attempts but fail all). Sure sign of unauthorized attemps to access.
